title: Compute brief - 11 November 2026
description: Demand is not the constraint; sites and financing are. Anthropic's amended IPO filing says its $34.9 billion August deal with Lambda is now terminable after Lambda missed a facility-lease deadline, while CoreWeave posted a $132.5 billion backlog and said slower construction could keep GPU prices higher for longer. Wire: Anthropic and Lambda, CoreWeave Q3, Google Malaysia $15 billion, Kraft Sutton 900 MW, Integra Quanah 756 MW, BNEF 181 GW on-site gas. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The contracts are signed. The sites are not.
lede: Anthropic's second IPO filing amendment, filed Tuesday, says its August 2026 compute agreement with Lambda, about $34.9 billion of a $41.3 billion set of Lambda commitments, is now terminable by either party because Lambda did not secure the facility lease by the contractual date; neither side has given notice and Anthropic says it does not intend to terminate. The same filing lifts its Microsoft commitment to at least $47.2 billion. Hours later CoreWeave reported Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168%, raised 2026 guidance and showed backlog of $132.5 billion, up from $104.2 billion in June, while saying it will avoid parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 at current yields. CEO Michael Intrator argued that if sector construction slows, installed compute gets scarcer and GPU pricing may stay higher for longer. TSMC's October revenue hit NT$586.9 billion, up 59.7% year on year and its highest month on record. BloombergNEF counts 181 GW of on-site gas proposed for data centres in the US and Europe as builders route around grid queues. Live list prices held for a third straight day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks and 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.
